candidate_local_claim: Under asymptotic inner-product preservation on a semigroup-stable dense domain and convergence of the corresponding semigroup matrix elements at t and 2t, the polarization identity yields strong semigroup convergence on that domain without exact isometric identifications or a finite net of the infinite-dimensional unit sphere.
cheap_falsifiers: If T(t)=exp(-tH), H>=0 self-adjoint, is an isometry for any t>0 on the whole Hilbert space, then H=0; hence an isometry claim is incompatible with nontrivial positive-energy excitations.
The unit sphere of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space has no finite delta-net for delta<1.
Weak matrix-element convergence plus uniform boundedness alone does not imply strong operator convergence; extra norm/semigroup information is required.
Any use of J_sigma on T(t)phi or resolvent vectors must prove the map/domain is defined there; asymptotic isometry on a dense cylinder domain is not an exact global isometry.
